To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the 5-HT(1) receptor blockade by SB-269970 produces antidepressant-like action in the rat forced swim test.

the 5-HT( 7) receptor antagonist SB-269970 and the tricyclic antidepressant imipramine produce a similar effect in the rat forced swim test, but the mechanism underlying the anti-immobilization action of SB-269 970 is different from that underlying the effect of imipramin e and seems to involve an increase in noradrenaline transmission in the rat prefrontal co r tex.
the 5-HT(1A) and 5-HT(2A) receptor antagonists, but not the 5-HT transporter blocker or the 5-HT (7) receptor antagonist, are able to reverse the immobility of rats exposed to the forced swim test.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the first demonstration of the antidepressant-like effect of a selective 5-HT (7) receptor antagonist in the forced swim paradigm.
the role of the 5-HT(6) receptor in the regulation of the activity of the nigrostriatal dopaminergic system in the rat.
the possibility of the 5-HT(1) receptor blockade as one of the new strategies of antidepressant drug therapy, and it also provides some new information on the mechanism of imipramines' action.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the antidepressant-like effects of SB-26970 in the forced swim paradigm are mediated by a complex mechanism involving the activation of 5-HT(2C) and 5-HT(6) receptor subtypes and the stimulation of DA, NA and possibly also 5-HT transmission, but not by the blockade of 5-HT1A, 5-HT1B, 5-HT(1D) and 5HT1E receptors.
5-HT(1A) and 5-HT(2) receptor antagonists are more promising candidates for the development of new antidepressant drugs than 5-HT(6) and 5HT(7) receptor antagonists.
the antidepressant-like effect of SB- 269970 is not mediated by the 5-HT(1A) or 5-HT(2A) receptors, but it may be due to the blockade of 5-HT(4), 5-HT(6) or 5- HT(7) receptors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the selective 5HT(7) receptor antagonists might be considered as potential candidates for the development of new antidepressants.
the 5-HT(1A) and 5-HT(6) receptors, but not 5-HT(2C) and 5- HT(7) receptors, are the main sites of the imipramine action in the prefrontc cortex of rats.

5-HT(2C) and 5-HT(1A) receptors are involved in imipramine-induced antidepressant effects, while 5-HT(3) and 5HT(7) receptors are involved, respectively, in the anti-immobilitary action of the selective 1A/7 receptor antagonist and imimpramine.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the 5-HT(2A) receptor agonist, DOI, and the 5-HT2A/2C receptor antagonist, M100907, are effective in the FST and that the 5- HT2C receptor is not required to elicit antidepressant-like effects in the FST.

the 5-HT(1A) and 5-HT(2C) receptors are involved in the regulation of anxiety and depression, and the selective 5HT(1A) or 5-HT(6) receptor antagonist may be useful in treating anxiety disorders and depression, respectively.
the blockade of 5-HT( 7) receptors by SB-269970 can potentiate the antidepressant-like effect of imipramines.
